name: regkv
description: Read a Windows registry hive with regipy: a key's values (each with its registry type and length, read whole: regipy's default cut to 256 characters is not taken), its subkeys with their last-written times (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits), and a bounded recursive listing. A reader, not a decoder: a binary value comes back as hex and nothing more, so UserAssist, ShimCache, BAM, SAM and ShellBag values are not decoded here. Completeness is said: unreadable keys and values are under problems, branches the walk did not enter (depth or node limit, or an error) under stopped_branches, and the whole recursive listing is kept in a file the answer names past the inline page; status is complete or partial (partial when a problem was named, a branch was not entered or the inline listing was cut) and status_basis says which. Every key listed is also in a file the answer names (all_subkeys) when the inline list of 2,000 is not the whole of it. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. The tool stops at its own time limit (27 seconds) with what it walked and names the branches it did not open; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Problems are a page (the first 50 inline, all in the file all_problems names); the names of a missing key's siblings are at most 200 (subkeys_there_count). A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. A value name that repeats is numbered once per name ('name (2)'). A big-endian DWORD is a problem (regipy returns no data for the type). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a value or a name, are counted (library_messages_withheld) and never printed. depth is 0 to 128; a key whose subkey list was already reached (a cycle, or a list two keys share) is named and not entered again; a key that declares more values than were read is a problem; a hive that is not a regular file (a named pipe) is not opened. hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ) and the transaction logs beside the hive are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so a dirty hive's newest state may be missing. SENSITIVE: values whose name says password, secret, token or credential (a DWORD or QWORD excepted), every value under Policy\Secrets, PolEKList and PolSecretEncryptionKey of a SECURITY hive, the cached logons (NL$) and the V value of each SAM user are replaced by a marker holding only their length and listed under sensitive_values_withheld; the type of a value never lets one through, and the place is judged by the key names the hive holds, not by the spelling asked for. No flag brings one back. A secret inside a value that does not look like one (a command line with a password in it, an ImagePath) is NOT recognised and comes back whole. The key path is read from the hive's root, a leading backslash or not. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). ORDER: the subkeys of a key, the keys of a recursive listing, the values of a key and the names listed when a key is not found are in the order of the TEXT SHOWN for each name (a placeholder is its own text), and withheld names in an order of their own that is new for every run. The order the hive stores them in is not kept: a hive stores a key's subkeys alphabetically by their raw names, so a withheld name listed where the hive puts it would sit between its neighbours and give away its first letter. What a listing is ordered by is only what the answer shows. Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (key names, value names and value data): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: 0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 (an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940, so the rate is small and not zero). The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

hive.description: Path to the registry hive file on disk (a copy; transaction logs beside it are named, not applied)

key.description: Registry key path, backslash form e.g. \Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion

depth.description: Levels below the key to open when recurse=true (default 2); a branch left closed is listed under stopped_branches

limit.description: Recursive nodes shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole listing is in the file named by all_nodes

max_nodes.description: Upper bound on the nodes a recursive walk visits (default 1000000); branches left past it are listed under stopped_branches

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
